metadata.title: Profiles of teaching practices and teacher co-operation: A person-centered approach in multilevel context

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses secondary microdata from TALIS 2018 Turkey at the upper-secondary level (ISCED 3), with the original TALIS sampling described as two-stage stratified sampling across participating countries. The analytic sample is restricted to teachers with complete responses on the instructional-practices indicators used for latent profile analysis and to schools with available school-characteristics data in the TALIS national database. The manuscript does not report applying TALIS sampling weights or any specific weight variable (e.g., teacher/student design weights) in the estimation of the multilevel latent profile analysis. Because the analysis is model-based (MLPA in Mplus) rather than a standard ML prediction pipeline, the paper’s weighting strategy is not documented; readers should treat the results as conditional on the analyzed subsample and consider whether population-representative weighting is needed for generalization.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the dependent variables are latent profile memberships and scale-based teacher practices/collaboration indicators from TALIS questionnaires, not cognitive achievement scores that TALIS/PISA-style PVs are designed to represent. The study imputes missingness for the LPA indicators and a level-1 covariate using multiple imputation, so missing-data handling is explicitly addressed for the questionnaire measures used to form profiles.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Data are drawn from TALIS 2018 Turkey at ISCED level 3 (upper secondary). Although TALIS-2018 Turkey includes 448 school principals and 8342 teachers from 457 schools, the analytic sample is restricted to teachers with non-missing data after examination for missingness. Teachers (n=1297) who did not respond to all items of the instructional-practices scales used as indicators of latent profile analysis were excluded. Additionally, teachers (n=184) working in schools without available school-characteristics data in the TALIS national database were excluded. The final analytic sample comprises 6861 teachers from 443 schools.

The analytic sample includes 6861 teachers from 443 schools after excluding teachers with missing responses on the instructional-practices indicators and excluding schools lacking school-characteristics data. The optimal solution was a five-profile model selected using AIC/BIC/aBIC, entropy, and the adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin test; posterior probabilities indicated low misclassification. Profile membership differences were examined with multinomial logistic regression using teacher-level predictors (gender, teaching experience, team innovativeness) and school-level covariates (school location, school size, support and administrative personnel ratios). The paper reports significant associations of team innovativeness with membership across profiles and significant effects of school location for some comparisons, while teacher experience showed no significant relationship with profile membership. Limitations include reliance on teacher self-reports for instructional practices and the absence of documented survey-weight application. data.outcome_summary: This study uses TALIS 2018 Turkey upper-secondary (ISCED 3) teacher questionnaire data to identify five latent teacher profiles based on instructional practices (clarity of instruction, cognitive activation, classroom management) and teacher co-operation, using multilevel latent profile analysis (MLPA) to account for teachers nested within schools. The analytic sample includes 6861 teachers from 443 schools after excluding teachers with missing responses on the instructional-practices indicators and excluding schools lacking school-characteristics data. The optimal solution was a five-profile model selected using AIC/BIC/aBIC, entropy, and the adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin test; posterior probabilities indicated low misclassification. Profile membership differences were examined with multinomial logistic regression using teacher-level predictors (gender, teaching experience, team innovativeness) and school-level covariates (school location, school size, support and administrative personnel ratios). The paper reports significant associations of team innovativeness with membership across profiles and significant effects of school location for some comparisons, while teacher experience showed no significant relationship with profile membership. Limitations include reliance on teacher self-reports for instructional practices and the absence of documented survey-weight application.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The study is a person-centered latent profiling analysis (single-level and multilevel latent profile analysis) rather than a machine-learning predictive modeling paper. As a result, it does not train or compare ML algorithms, and there are no supervised target variables with ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) to populate main_findings. The outcomes are latent profile memberships and their associations with covariates, which are handled via MLPA and multinomial logistic regression in Mplus rather than ML prediction pipelines.
